title: Destructuring
summary: Destructuring is syntax for unpacking values from arrays or properties from objects into individual variables. Object destructuring matches by property name; array destructuring matches by position. You can rename variables, provide default values, nest destructuring, and skip elements. It is commonly used with function parameters, API responses, and any function that returns an array or object.
keyPoints: Object destructuring: const { title, year } = movie — matches by property name
Array destructuring: const [first, second] = arr — matches by position
Rename while destructuring: const { title: movieTitle } = movie
Default values: const { tagline = 'No tagline' } = movie
Nested destructuring: const { director: { name } } = movie — director is NOT extracted as a variable
Skip array elements: const [first, , third] = arr
Destructure in function parameters: function display({ title, rating }) {}
Functions returning arrays can be unpacked directly: const [min, max] = getRange()

exercises.explanation: Object destructuring uses {} and matches by property name. Array destructuring uses [] and matches by position — objects are not arrays.
Nested destructuring goes into director and extracts name. Note: director is NOT declared as a variable here — only name is.

exercises.prompt:
Given:
const genres = ['Action', 'Sci-Fi', 'Thriller']

How do you skip 'Sci-Fi' and get only 'Action' and 'Thriller'?
exercises.explanation: An empty slot (consecutive commas with nothing between) skips that position in array destructuring.

exercises.prompt: A function receives a single movie object with title and rating properties. Which signature correctly destructures those properties from the parameter?
exercises.explanation: When a function receives an object, you can destructure its properties directly in the parameter list. This is equivalent to writing const { title, rating } = movie inside the function body.

exercises.prompt:
Given:
const movie = { title: 'Unknown' }
const { title: movieTitle, tagline = 'No tagline' } = movie

What are the values of movieTitle and tagline?
exercises.explanation: title is renamed to movieTitle and gets the value 'Unknown'. tagline does not exist on movie, so it falls back to the default 'No tagline'.

exercises.prompt: A function getRange() returns a two-element array: [min, max]. How do you destructure it into variables named low and high?
exercises.explanation: Array destructuring uses [] and matches by position, not by name. You can choose any variable names — low and high don't need to match anything inside the function.

exercises.prompt:
Given:
const movie = { title: 'Unknown Film' }  // no tagline property

Which uses destructuring syntax to provide a default value of 'No tagline available' for tagline?
exercises.explanation: Destructuring default values use = inside the braces. The default applies when the property is undefined (missing). Option A also works but is not destructuring syntax. Option C is invalid syntax — : renames the variable, not sets a default.

exercises.prompt:
Given:
const movie = { title: 'Inception', director: { name: 'Christopher Nolan' } }
const { director: { name: directorName } } = movie

After this statement, which variables are declared?
options: Neither — nested destructuring must be done in separate steps
exercises.explanation: In nested destructuring, director is a pattern used to drill into the object — it is NOT declared as a variable. Only directorName is declared and holds the value 'Christopher Nolan'.

exercises.prompt:
Given:
const genres = ['Action', 'Sci-Fi', 'Thriller']

Which line destructures the first genre and collects the remaining genres into a new array?
exercises.explanation: The rest element (...) in array destructuring collects everything after the named positions. Here first = 'Action' and remainingGenres = ['Sci-Fi', 'Thriller'].

exercises.prompt:
You need to swap existing variables a and b without a temporary variable:
let a = 'Action'
let b = 'Comedy'

Which expression swaps them correctly?
exercises.explanation: Array destructuring can swap two variables in one line. The right side creates a temporary array [b, a], then the left side assigns those values back. Using const (option C) would declare new variables instead of reassigning the existing ones.
